section.title: org.osgi.service.transaction.control
section.para: Transaction Control Service Package Version 1.0.

Bundles wishing to use this package must list the package in the Import-Package header of the bundle's manifest. This package has two types of users: the consumers that use the API in this package and the providers that implement the API in this package.

section.title: public abstract class TransactionBuilder implements TransactionStarter
section.para: A builder for a piece of transactional work

formalpara.title: Provider Type
formalpara.para: Consumers of this API must not implement this type

section.title: protected final List<Class<? extends Throwable>> noRollbackFor
section.para: The list of Throwable types that must not trigger rollback

section.title: protected final List<Class<? extends Throwable>> rollbackFor
section.para: The list of Throwable types that must trigger rollback

section.title: public final TransactionBuilder noRollbackFor(Class<? extends Throwable> t, Class<? extends Throwable>... throwables)

formalpara.title: t
formalpara.para: An exception type that should not trigger rollback

formalpara.title: throwables
formalpara.para: further exception types that should not trigger rollback

section.para: Declare a list of Exception types (and their subtypes) that must not trigger a rollback. By default the transaction will rollback for all Exceptions. If an Exception type is registered using this method then that type and its subtypes will not trigger rollback. If the same type is registered using both rollbackFor(Class, Class...) and noRollbackFor(Class, Class...) then the transaction will not begin and will instead throw a TransactionException
Note that the behavior of this method differs from Java EE and Spring in two ways:

listitem.para: In Java EE and Spring transaction management checked exceptions are considered "normal returns" and do not trigger rollback. Using an Exception as a normal return value is considered a bad design practice. In addition this means that checked Exceptions such as java.sql.SQLException do not trigger rollback by default. This, in turn, leads to implementation mistakes that break the transactional behavior of applications.

In Java EE it is legal to specify the same Exception type in rollbackFor and noRollbackFor. Stating that the same Exception should both trigger and not trigger rollback is a logical impossibility, and clearly indicates an API usage error. This API therefore enforces usage by triggering an exception in this invalid case.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: this builder

section.title: public abstract TransactionBuilder readOnly()
section.para: Indicate to the Transaction Control service that this transaction will be read-only. This hint may be used by the Transaction Control service and associated resources to optimize the transaction.
Note that this method is for optimization purposes only. The TransactionControl service is free to ignore the call if it does not offer read-only optimization.

If a transaction is marked read-only and then the scoped work performs a write operation on a resource then this is a programming error. The resource is free to raise an exception when the write is attempted, or to permit the write operation. As a result the transaction may commit successfully, or may rollback.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: this builder

section.title: public final TransactionBuilder rollbackFor(Class<? extends Throwable> t, Class<? extends Throwable>... throwables)

formalpara.title: throwables
formalpara.para: The Exception types that should trigger rollback

section.para: Declare a list of Exception types (and their subtypes) that must trigger a rollback. By default the transaction will rollback for all Exceptions. If a more specific type is registered using noRollbackFor(Class, Class...) then that type will not trigger rollback. If the same type is registered using both rollbackFor(Class, Class...) and noRollbackFor(Class, Class...) then the transaction will not begin and will instead throw a TransactionException
Note that the behavior of this method differs from Java EE and Spring in two ways:

listitem.para: In Java EE and Spring transaction management checked exceptions are considered "normal returns" and do not trigger rollback. Using an Exception as a normal return value is considered a bad design practice. In addition this means that checked Exceptions such as java.sql.SQLException do not trigger rollback by default. This, in turn, leads to implementation mistakes that break the transactional behavior of applications.

In Java EE it is legal to specify the same Exception type in rollbackFor and noRollbackFor. Stating that the same Exception should both trigger and not trigger rollback is a logical impossibility, and clearly indicates an API usage error. This API therefore enforces usage by triggering an exception in this invalid case.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: this builder

section.title: public void postCompletion(Consumer<TransactionStatus> job) throws IllegalStateException
section.para: Register a callback that will be made after the scope completes
For transactional scopes the state of the scope will be either TransactionStatus.COMMITTED or TransactionStatus.ROLLED_BACK.
For no-transaction scopes the state of the scope will always be TransactionStatus.NO_TRANSACTION.
Post-completion callbacks should not throw Exceptions and cannot affect the outcome of a piece of scoped work

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: IllegalStateException– if no transaction is active

section.title: public void preCompletion(Runnable job) throws IllegalStateException

formalpara.title: job
formalpara.para: The action to perform before completing the scope

section.para: Register a callback that will be made before a scope completes.

For transactional scopes the state of the scope will be either TransactionStatus.ACTIVE or TransactionStatus.MARKED_ROLLBACK. Pre-completion callbacks may call setRollbackOnly() to prevent a commit from proceeding.
For no-transaction scopes the state of the scope will always be TransactionStatus.NO_TRANSACTION.
Exceptions thrown by pre-completion callbacks are treated as if they were thrown by the scoped work, including any configured commit or rollback behaviors for transactional scopes.

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: IllegalStateException– if the transaction has already passed beyond the TransactionStatus.MARKED_ROLLBACK state

section.title: public T notSupported(Callable<T> work) throws TransactionException, ScopedWorkException
section.para: The supplied piece of work must be run outside the context of a transaction. If an existing transaction is active then it must be suspended and a "no transaction" context associated with the work. After the work has completed any suspended transaction must be resumed.

The "no transaction" context does not support resource enlistment, and will not commit or rollback any changes, however it does provide a post completion callback to any registered functions. This function is suitable for final cleanup, such as closing a connection

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The value returned by the work

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionException– if there is an error starting or completing the transaction

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: ScopedWorkException– if the supplied work throws an Exception

section.title: public T required(Callable<T> work) throws TransactionException, TransactionRolledBackException, ScopedWorkException
section.para: A transaction is required to run the supplied piece of work. If no transaction is active then it must be started and associated with the work and then completed after the transactional work has finished.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The value returned by the work

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionException– if there is an error starting or completing the transaction

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionRolledBackException– if the transaction rolled back due to a failure in one of the resources or an internal error in the TransactionControl service

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: ScopedWorkException– if the supplied work throws an Exception

section.title: public T requiresNew(Callable<T> work) throws TransactionException, TransactionRolledBackException, ScopedWorkException
section.para: A new transaction is required to run the supplied piece of work. If an existing transaction is active then it must suspended and a new transaction started and associated with the work. After the work has completed the new transaction must also complete and any suspended transaction be resumed.

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The value returned by the work

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionException– if there is an error starting or completing the transaction

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionRolledBackException– if the transaction rolled back due to a failure

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: ScopedWorkException– if the supplied work throws an Exception

section.title: public T supports(Callable<T> work) throws TransactionException, ScopedWorkException
section.para: The supplied piece of work may run inside or outside the context of a transaction. If an existing transaction or "no transaction" context is active then it will continue, otherwise a new "no transaction" context is associated with the work. After the work has completed any created transaction context must be completed.

The "no transaction" context does not support resource enlistment, and will not commit or rollback any changes, however it does provide a post completion callback to any registered functions. This function is suitable for final cleanup, such as closing a connection

formalpara.title: Returns
formalpara.para: The value returned by the work

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: TransactionException– if there is an error starting or completing the transaction

formalpara.title: Throws
formalpara.para: ScopedWorkException– if the supplied work throws an Exception

section.title: enum TransactionStatus
section.para: The status of the transaction A transaction may not enter all of the states in this enum, however it will always traverse the enum in ascending order. In particular if the TransactionStatus is reported as X then it will never proceed into a state Y where X.compareTo(Y) >= 0;

section.title: NO_TRANSACTION
section.para: No transaction is currently active

section.title: ACTIVE
section.para: A transaction is currently in progress

section.title: MARKED_ROLLBACK
section.para: A transaction is currently in progress and has been marked for rollback

section.title: PREPARING
section.para: A two phase commit is occurring and the transaction is being prepared

section.title: PREPARED
section.para: A two phase commit is occurring and the transaction has been prepared

section.title: COMMITTING
section.para: The transaction is in the process of being committed

section.title: COMMITTED
section.para: The transaction has committed

section.title: ROLLING_BACK
section.para: The transaction is in the process of rolling back

section.title: ROLLED_BACK
section.para: The transaction has been rolled back
